mainTopic: How the משנה in מסכת שבת and the משנה in מסכת שבועות count the cases of carrying on שבת, and what 'יציאות' includes
overview: This amud finishes quoting a list from the משנה in מסכת שבועות: ידיעות הטומאה, מראות נגעים, and יציאות השבת, each called 'two that are four.' The גמרא asks why our משנה counts carrying on שבת as eight cases (four inside, four outside) while שבועות counts only four. A first answer, that שבת lists אבות and תולדות, fails on the count. רב פפא answers instead that מסכת שבת lists liable and exempt cases, while שבועות lists only the four liable ones. The גמרא then explains these four as two of הוצאה and two of הכנסה. When it asks how bringing in can be called 'יציאות,' רב אשי says the תנא calls any moving of an object from its place 'הוצאה.' He proves this from a משנה, and רבינא proves it from our own משנה. רבא instead reads the text as 'רשויות שבת.' Finally, רב מתנה challenges אביי that the משנה's eight cases are really twelve. אביי replies that by that logic there would be sixteen, and רב מתנה begins a defense that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The שבועות list continues: awareness of impurity and leprosy signs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא keeps quoting the משנה in מסכת שבועות. It lists ידיעות הטומאה and מראות נגעים, and each one is 'two that are four.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Awareness of impurity: two that are four. Signs of נגעים: two that are four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the list from the משנה in מסכת שבועות. These items are background that leads up to the item that matters for our sugya.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every item on this list follows one pattern: two main cases, plus two more cases that come from them, for four in total. For ידיעות הטומאה, the four cases are ways a person was unaware while eating קודש or entering the מקדש. Either he forgot his own טומאה, or he forgot that the food was קודש or that the place was the מקדש. For מראות נגעים, the two Torah signs, בהרת and שאת, each have a secondary shade.

keyTerms.meaning: Cases of awareness and forgetting of one's impure status, which can lead to a קרבן
The appearances or shades of צרעת afflictions
Two that are four: two main cases with two derived cases

steps.confusionAlert: This is not our משנה in מסכת שבת. It is a list quoted from מסכת שבועות. These items are not the topic of our sugya. They are quoted only because they share the 'two that are four' pattern.

phrases.english: Awareness of ritual impurity:
two that are four.
Signs of leprous afflictions:
two that are four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quotation of the משנה in שבועות that the גמרא began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the משנה in שבועות, ידיעות הטומאה and מראות נגעים are each counted as two main cases that become four.

steps.title: The שבועות list includes carrying out on שבת as two that are four
steps.stepSummary: The משנה in שבועות also lists יציאות השבת as 'two that are four.' This is the item that connects to our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Acts of carrying out on שבת: two that are four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches the item on the שבועות list that matters for us: carrying out on שבת. This line sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here מסכת שבועות counts יציאות השבת as only four. Our משנה in מסכת שבת counts them as four inside plus four outside, which is eight. That gap in the count is what the גמרא will ask about next.

keyTerms.meaning: Acts of carrying or transferring between domains on שבת

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the exact line that will be compared with our משנה. The whole question that follows grows out of it.

phrases.english: Acts of carrying out on Shabbat:
two that are four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the quoted list and arrives at the item that will be compared with our משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה in שבועות counts יציאות השבת as two that are four, with no mention of 'inside' and 'outside.'

steps.title: Why does our משנה count eight but the שבועות משנה only four?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why our משנה says 'two that are four inside and two that are four outside,' while the משנה in שבועות says only 'two that are four.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different here, where the משנה teaches 'two that are four inside and two that are four outside,' and what is different there, where it teaches only 'two that are four' and nothing more?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts the two משניות side by side and points out that they count the same melachah differently. It wants an explanation for the difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both משניות are about the same topic, carrying on שבת. Yet our משנה counts both the person standing inside and the person standing outside, for eight cases. The משנה in שבועות stops at four. The גמרא asks what each משנה is focusing on that makes it count differently.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? A formula that asks why two similar cases are treated differently
Here, meaning our משנה in מסכת שבת
There, meaning the משנה in מסכת שבועות

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying either משנה is wrong. It is asking why the two counts differ. The answer in the next step explains what each משנה is focused on.

phrases.english: What is different here, that it teaches
"two that are four inside
and two that are four outside,"
and what is different there, that it teaches
"two that are four," and nothing more?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the item quoted in step 2 and contrasts it with the wording of our משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The different counts of יציאות השבת in our משנה (eight) and in the משנה in שבועות (four).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two משניות on the same subject should count it the same way. Since they don't, some difference in focus must be explained.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What each משנה is focused on that explains why one counts eight cases and the other counts four.

steps.title: First answer: our tractate lists main and sub-categories
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה is the main home of הלכות שבת, so it teaches both אבות and תולדות. The משנה in שבועות is not, so it teaches only the אבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, in מסכת שבת, which is the main place for שבת laws, the משנה teaches the main categories and the sub-categories. There, in שבועות, which is not the main place for שבת, it teaches only the main categories and not the sub-categories.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 3. Our משנה is longer because מסכת שבת is the 'home base' for שבת laws, so it lists everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying out (הוצאה) is an אב, a main category. Bringing in (הכנסה) is a תולדה, a sub-category. Our משנה teaches both, which is why its count is longer. The משנה in שבועות only mentions שבת in passing, so it lists just the אבות.

keyTerms.meaning: The main place where the laws of שבת are taught (מסכת שבת)
Main categories of forbidden work on שבת
Sub-categories, forbidden acts that come from a main category
Here (our משנה) / there (the משנה in שבועות)

phrases.english: Here, where it is the main place of Shabbat laws,
it teaches the main categories and teaches the sub-categories.
phrases.notes: אבות = carrying out; תולדות = bringing in

phrases.english: There, where it is not the main place of Shabbat laws,
it teaches the main categories, but does not teach the sub-categories.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא דְּעִיקַּר שַׁבָּת הוּא, תָּנֵי אָבוֹת וְתָנֵי תּוֹלָדוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the difference in wording by the purpose of each מסכת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות should list the same number of cases
steps.terutzMaskana: שבת lists אבות and תולדות; שבועות lists only אבות

steps.title: The main acts of carrying out are only two
steps.stepSummary: If שבועות lists only the אבות, meaning carrying out, there are only two such cases. So how can שבועות call them 'two that are four'?
steps.simpleTranslation: What are the main categories? The acts of carrying out. But there are only two acts of carrying out!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. If שבועות counts only carrying out, the number does not reach four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are only two liable ways to carry out. The בעל הבית can hand an object out to the poor man, or the poor man can take it from the house and carry it out. So 'four' cannot mean only carrying out, and the first answer runs into a counting problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Acts of carrying out from a private area to a public one

phrases.english: The main categories, what are they?
Acts of carrying out.
But acts of carrying out are only two!
phrases.notes: Where are the other two to make 'four'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָבוֹת מַאי נִיהוּ? יְצִיאוֹת, וִיצִיאוֹת תְּרֵי הָוְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of Step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שבועות lists only the אבות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only two liable acts of carrying out exist, but שבועות says 'four'

steps.title: Exempt cases cannot fill out the four
steps.stepSummary: A possible fix is that שבועות's four include some liable and some exempt cases. This is rejected, because שבועות compares the list to מראות נגעים, where all four cases count.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that some of the four are liable and some are exempt, that cannot be. The משנה teaches this alongside the signs of נגעים. Just as there all four count, so too here all four must be liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a possible way out of its question. You cannot reach four by adding exempt cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might add the two 'half-act' cases where you are פטור to reach four. But the משנה in שבועות lists יציאות right next to מראות נגעים, and all four signs of נגעים truly count. So all four יציאות in שבועות must be cases of real חיוב, and the question from Step 5 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introducing a possible answer)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. The גמרא is closing off a possible answer to the question in Step 5, so that question still stands.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא, מֵהֶן לְחִיּוּב וּמֵהֶן לִפְטוּר,
phrases.english: And if you say: some of them are for liability and some of them are for exemption,
but it teaches it parallel to the signs of affliction:
just as there, all of them are for liability,
so too here, all of them are for liability!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, מֵהֶן לְחִיּוּב וּמֵהֶן לִפְטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects a possible answer to Step 5, strengthening the question
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that שבועות's four include exempt cases
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The parallel to מראות נגעים shows that every item on the list must be a real חיוב

steps.title: רב פפא: our tractate lists liable and exempt cases
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a new answer. מסכת שבת teaches both חיובי and פטורי, eight in all. שבועות teaches only the four liable cases. The גמרא spells out which four these are in Step 10.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: Here, in the main place for שבת laws, it teaches the liable cases and the exempt cases. There, where it is not the main place for שבת, it teaches the liable cases but not the exempt cases.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first answer failed, רב פפא replaces it. The difference between the two משניות is liable cases versus exempt cases, not אבות versus תולדות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שבועות, the 'four' are all liable: two of carrying out and two of bringing in. This fits the parallel to נגעים. Our משנה adds the four exempt 'half-act' cases on top, which makes eight.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the new answer
Cases of liability and cases of exemption

steps.whatToRemember: Final answer (רב פפא): שבועות lists the four liable cases (two carrying out, two bringing in). Our משנה lists those four plus four exempt cases, eight in total.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that bringing in (הכנסה) is a full חיוב, counted together with carrying out. It also shows that our משנה teaches cases that are פטור too.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
Here, where it is the main place of Shabbat laws,
it teaches cases of liability and cases of exemption.
There, where it is not the main place of Shabbat laws,
it teaches cases of liability but does not teach cases of exemption.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed answer of Step 4 with a new explanation
steps.terutzResolutionType: New answer that avoids the counting problem
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference is אבות versus תולדות
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference is liable cases versus exempt cases; שבועות's four are all liable

steps.title: What are the liable cases in שבועות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the liable cases (חיובי) in שבועות are, and first suggests they are cases of carrying out (יציאות).
steps.simpleTranslation: What are the liable cases? Cases of carrying out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is checking רב פפא's answer by asking what exactly the 'liable cases' in שבועות are. The first answer is: carrying out. This sets up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא said שבועות lists only the four liable cases. The משנה in שבועות calls them 'יציאות,' so the natural guess is that they are all cases of carrying out.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable cases, where a person must bring a קרבן
Acts of carrying out (from a private area to a public area)

phrases.english: What are the liable cases?
Cases of carrying out.
phrases.notes: Based on the word 'יציאות' in the משנה in שבועות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Probes the details of רב פפא's answer from Step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which cases count as the 'liable' cases listed in שבועות.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: First suggestion: they are cases of carrying out (יציאות).

steps.title: Carrying out gives only two cases
steps.stepSummary: If the liable cases are only carrying out, there are just two of them, not four.
steps.simpleTranslation: But carrying out is only two cases!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects: if we count only carrying out, we get just two liable cases, not the four that שבועות mentions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case of a person inside and a person outside, only two liable acts are carrying out: one by the person inside and one by the person outside. So 'יציאות' alone cannot add up to 'four.'

phrases.english: Cases of carrying out are only two!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the four liable cases in שבועות are all carrying out.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Carrying out gives only two liable cases, so the count of four fails.

steps.title: Two of carrying out and two of bringing in
steps.stepSummary: The four liable cases are two of carrying out (הוצאה) and two of bringing in (הכנסה).
steps.simpleTranslation: Two cases of carrying out and two cases of bringing in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the four liable cases are not all carrying out. Two are carrying out and two are bringing in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding the two cases of bringing in (from public to private) to the two cases of carrying out makes four. This fills in רב פפא's answer from Step 7, which said only that שבועות lists the liable cases without naming them.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying out, from private to public
Bringing in, from public to private

phrases.english: Two of carrying out
and two of bringing in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All four liable cases must be carrying out, so only two exist.
steps.terutzMaskana: The four are two of הוצאה and two of הכנסה.

steps.title: But the משנה says 'carrying out'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה in שבועות uses the word 'יציאות,' not bringing in, so how can bringing in be counted?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה teaches 'carrying out'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: the משנה in שבועות clearly says 'יציאות,' carrying out. So how can we say half the cases are bringing in?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 10 fixes the number, but it seems to clash with the wording. Bringing in is not carrying out, so the word 'יציאות' should not cover it.

phrases.english: But it teaches 'carrying out'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 10 from the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: Counting bringing in among the 'יציאות' of שבועות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'יציאות' means carrying out, so it should not include bringing in.

steps.title: The תנא calls bringing in 'carrying out' too
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the תנא also uses the word 'הוצאה' for bringing in.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The תנא also calls bringing in 'carrying out.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers that the word 'הוצאה' in the language of the משנה is broad and also covers bringing in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was only about the word. רב אשי shows the word does not mean only 'taking outside.' It can mean bringing in as well, so 'יציאות' covers all four cases.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב אשי is changing the law. Bringing in is still bringing in. He is only explaining that the משנה uses the word 'הוצאה' as a general name for both kinds of moving.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The tanna also calls bringing in 'carrying out.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי תַּנָּא הַכְנָסָה נָמֵי הוֹצָאָה קָרֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of Step 11.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the תנא's language, 'הוצאה' includes הכנסה too.

steps.title: Proof from 'one who carries from domain to domain'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves רב אשי's claim from a משנה that says 'המוציא מרשות לרשות חייב,' which also covers bringing in.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? From what we learned: One who carries out from one domain to another is liable. Aren't we also dealing with someone bringing in from the public domain to the private domain, and still it calls it 'carrying out'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for רב אשי's idea and brings one: a משנה that uses the word 'מוציא' for moving between any two domains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'from one domain to another' without saying which way. That must include moving from רשות הרבים into רשות היחיד, which is bringing in. Yet the משנה still calls it 'מוציא,' so the word clearly covers bringing in.

keyTerms.meaning: From what we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: From where do we know this?
From what we learned in a mishna:
One who carries out from one domain to another is liable.
Are we not dealing with a case
where he brings in from the public domain
to the private domain,
and still it calls it 'carrying out'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי מִדִּתְנַן הַמּוֹצִיא מֵרְשׁוּת לִרְשׁוּת חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support רב אשי's answer in Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's claim that the תנא calls הכנסה 'הוצאה.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה 'המוציא מרשות לרשות חייב,' which must include bringing in from רשות הרבים to רשות היחיד.

steps.title: Why call bringing in 'carrying out'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason the תנא uses the word 'הוצאה' for bringing in.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know the תנא does this, the גמרא asks why. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof showed that the word is used this way. The גמרא now wants to understand the logic behind using 'carrying out' for moving in.

phrases.english: And what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the usage proven in Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the term 'הוצאה' is used for bringing in.

steps.title: Any lifting of an object from its place is 'carrying out'
steps.stepSummary: The תנא calls any lifting of an object from its place (and moving it to another domain) 'הוצאה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Any lifting of an object from its place, the תנא calls 'carrying out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that 'הוצאה' means taking an object out of its place, no matter which direction it goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word does not mean 'taking out of the house.' It means 'taking out of its place.' When you lift an object from רשות הרבים and bring it into a house, you are also taking it out of its place, so it is called הוצאה.
steps.whatToRemember: In משנה language, 'הוצאה' is a general name for moving an object from one domain to another. So the four 'יציאות' in שבועות are two of carrying out and two of bringing in, and all four are liable.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the מלאכה of carrying on שבת is usually called 'הוצאה' even though it includes bringing in. The main act is lifting the object from its place.

phrases.english: Any lifting of an object from its place
the tanna calls it 'carrying out.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל עֲקִירַת חֵפֶץ מִמְּקוֹמוֹ תַּנָּא הוֹצָאָה קָרֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'הוצאה' means taking an object out of its place, which includes bringing in.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The term 'יציאות' in שבועות covers both הוצאה and הכנסה, giving four liable cases.

steps.title: רבינא: Our own משנה shows that 'carrying out' includes bringing in
steps.stepSummary: רבינא supports רב אשי. Our משנה opens with the heading 'יציאות' but its very first case is one of bringing in. So the word 'יציאות' must include הכנסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Our משנה is also precise and shows the same thing. It says 'acts of carrying out,' and right away it describes a case of bringing in. We can learn from this that 'carrying out' includes bringing in.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא adds a second proof that the תנא uses the language of 'carrying out' even for bringing in. He takes this proof from our own משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה opens with the heading 'יציאות השבת.' Its first case, though, is the עני reaching in and putting an object into the hand of the בעל הבית, which is bringing in. Since the תנא lists bringing in right under the heading 'יציאות,' that heading must cover both directions.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, the one this גמרא is explaining
Is precise; its exact wording proves the point
Bringing an object in from רשות הרבים to רשות היחיד
Learn from this; the point is proven

steps.whatToRemember: The conclusion is that the תנא's word 'יציאות' / 'הוצאה' covers both carrying out and bringing in, because it means moving an object from one domain to another.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Our mishnah is also precise (and shows this),
for it teaches 'acts of carrying out,'
phrases.notes: This is the heading of our משנה: יציאות השבת.

phrases.english: and it immediately spells out a case of bringing in.
phrases.notes: The first case: the עני puts an object into the hand of the בעל הבית inside.

phrases.english: Conclude from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof, from our own משנה, for רב אשי's answer that 'הוצאה' includes bringing in.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's claim that the תנא calls bringing in 'הוצאה' / 'יציאות'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה lists a case of bringing in right under the heading 'יציאות השבת'.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'יציאות' in the language of the תנא includes הכנסה.

steps.title: רבא: The משנה actually reads 'domains,' not 'carrying out'
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the question from step 11 differently. The משנה's real wording is 'רשויות שבת שתים', meaning the domains of שבת are two. That wording naturally includes both carrying out and bringing in.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The משנה teaches 'domains.' It says: 'The domains of Shabbat are two.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a different answer to the question of how bringing in can be counted under 'יציאות.' He says the correct wording of the משנה is 'רשויות' (domains), so there is no problem in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי kept the word 'יציאות' and widened its meaning. רבא removes the problem a different way: he reads the text as 'רשויות.' The phrase 'the domains of שבת' fits any movement between domains, whether out or in.

keyTerms.meaning: Domains, areas of different legal status for carrying on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not disagreeing about the הלכה. Everyone agrees that bringing in is forbidden and counted. He only disagrees about the wording of the משנה.

phrases.english: Rava said,
it teaches 'domains':
'The domains of Shabbat are two.'
phrases.notes: רבא's version of the text, in place of 'יציאות השבת שתים'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent answer to the קשיא in step 11, in place of רב אשי's approach.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual emendation: the problem word is replaced by the correct reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה says 'יציאות,' which seems to mean carrying out only.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה says 'רשויות,' which covers movement in both directions between the domains.

steps.title: רב מתנה: The משנה says eight cases, but there are twelve
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה challenges אביי about the count in our משנה. The משנה says 'two that are four inside and two that are four outside,' which makes eight. But in the cases where each person does half the action, both people do something, so you can count twelve.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said to אביי: Are these eight? They are twelve!
steps.whatsHappening: A new discussion begins. רב מתנה questions the number of cases the משנה gives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's count adds up to eight: four inside and four outside. In the four later cases, the עני and the בעל הבית each do part of the act, one lifting and one putting down. If you count each person's action separately, those four cases become eight, and the total becomes twelve.

phrases.english: Rav Mattana said to Abaye:
Are these (only) eight?
phrases.notes: Two that are four inside, plus two that are four outside.

phrases.english: They are twelve!
phrases.notes: In the four 'half-and-half' cases, each person's action is counted separately: 4 + 8 = 12.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מַתְנָה לְאַבָּיֵי: הָא תַּמְנֵי הָוְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the wording question ('יציאות') to a new question about how the cases in the משנה are counted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's count: 'two that are four inside and two that are four outside' (eight).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If every person's action counts, the four shared cases each contain two actions. That gives twelve, not eight.

steps.title: אביי: By your logic, there would be sixteen
steps.stepSummary: אביי pushes back with a counter-question. If you count each person's part, then even in the first four cases the second person, who receives or hands over the object, also does something. That would make sixteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי answered: According to your reasoning, they would be sixteen!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי does not answer directly. He pushes back with a counter-question to show that רב מתנה's way of counting seems to go too far. In the next step רב מתנה defends his count of twelve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first four cases, one person does the whole act, but another person is also involved. That person either hands over the object or takes it. If every person involved is counted, those four cases also double, giving 8 + 8 = 16. אביי's point is that רב מתנה's method seems to prove too much. רב מתנה will answer this in the next step.
steps.confusionAlert: This is a 'your logic proves too much' move. It is not אביי's own count of the cases. רב מתנה answers it in the next step by showing why his count of twelve does not force sixteen.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, they are sixteen!
phrases.notes: Even in the first four cases, the passive second person (the one receiving or handing over) would also count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב מתנה's challenge with a counter-question that shows his counting method proves too much.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב מתנה's method of counting each person's action separately.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That method would seem to double the first four cases as well, giving sixteen. רב מתנה then disputes that his method leads there.

steps.title: רב מתנה says the count of sixteen is not a real problem
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה tells אביי that the counter-question ("then count sixteen") does not hurt his count of twelve. He opens his explanation with the word בשלמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said to אביי: That is not difficult, because granted…
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנה is answering אביי's pushback and says the problem of "sixteen" goes away. He only starts his reason here, so this line sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 19 אביי argued that if you count every person who does something, you should also count the second person in the first four cases, which makes sixteen. רב מתנה says this does not follow. The word בשלמא means "I agree it works in one set of cases." He is about to show why the first four cases are different from the half-and-half cases.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to him. Here רב מתנה is speaking to אביי.
That is not difficult. The speaker is about to remove the problem.
Granted, or it makes sense that… It accepts one side before showing that the other side is different.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop at בשלמא as if the answer is finished. The word only opens a comparison: "granted here… but there…". The real reason comes in the next lines.

phrases.english: He (Rav Mattana) said to him (Abaye): That is not difficult:
phrases.notes: רב מתנה rejects אביי's challenge of sixteen.

phrases.english: Granted,
phrases.notes: Opens a contrast. The explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's counter-question in step 19 and defends the count of twelve from step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between cases. רב מתנה will show that the first four cases are not like the half-and-half cases, so his counting does not force sixteen.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If you count both people in the half-and-half cases, you must also count the second person in the first four cases, which makes sixteen.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sixteen problem is not a real difficulty. The reason, which starts with בשלמא, separates the two kinds of cases.
